reason: Conversation 2 went straight to the correct diagnosis (dirty contacts on dock and robot), told the homeowner to unplug the base before cleaning, and the problem was resolved in one exchange without any unnecessary part talk, matching the hidden truth exactly. Conversation 1 eventually got to the same fix but buried it in long lists, repeatedly pushed the 'ageing battery' and battery-replacement angle (including a pointless battery-door teardown as the 'most likely fix') before contacts were even checked, and needed the homeowner to ask 'which should I try first?' before prioritising the obvious grubby contacts. Conversation 1 did ask for the exact error text and gave safety caveats, but its over-weighting of a battery purchase on a no-part-needed fault and its inefficiency make 2 the clearly better service.
